mainTopic: Honoring a כלה (praising her, dancing before her, giving her the right of way) and honoring Torah scholars
overview: This amud is about honoring a כלה and honoring Torah scholars. It opens with בית שמאי and בית הלל arguing over how to praise a bride. בית הלל say every כלה is called 'fair and graceful,' because once a choice is made you praise it and do not hurt anyone's feelings. The גמרא then brings songs of praise sung for brides in ארץ ישראל, songs sung when rabbis received סמיכה, and the song the emperor's maids sang for רבי אבהו. Next come stories of sages who danced before brides, including רב שמואל בר רב יצחק, whose juggling earned him a pillar of fire at his death, and רב אחא, who allowed carrying a bride only for someone to whom she is like a wooden beam. The גמרא rejects רבי יונתן's permission to look at a bride's face. It teaches that a funeral gives way to a bride and both give way to a king, and it explains why אגריפס was praised for yielding. It ends by teaching that one stops Torah study to escort the dead or a bride, and it measures how big a crowd is 'enough.' That last discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two ways to praise a bride
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say to praise the כלה as she really is. בית הלל say every כלה is called 'fair and graceful.'
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי: describe the bride as she is. בית הלל: say 'a fair and graceful bride.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the two opinions on what to sing when dancing before a כלה. The opening words are the end of בית שמאי's view, which started just before this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי want the praise to match the truth, so you praise the real good points she has. בית הלל use one standard praise for every bride, no matter what she is like. The next steps explain why each side holds this.
steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not saying to mention a bride's faults. They mean you praise the real good qualities she has, and nothing false.

phrases.english: A bride as she is.
And Beit Hillel say:
"A fair and graceful bride."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the question (begun before this section) of how one dances before a bride.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: praise the bride by her true qualities. בית הלל: call every bride 'fair and graceful.'

steps.title: Isn't that a lie?
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי ask: if the bride is lame or blind, how can you call her fair and graceful? The תורה says to stay far from falsehood.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is lame or blind, do you still say 'fair and graceful'? The תורה says, 'Keep far from a false matter'!
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי attack בית הלל's view with a hard case: a bride who has a clear defect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's praise is the same for every bride. So in a case where it is plainly untrue, it seems to break the פסוק that commands us to stay away from lies.

keyTerms.meaning: Keep far from a false matter (פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל:
phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:
In a case where she was lame or blind,
do they say about her: "A fair and graceful bride"?
But the Torah said: "Keep far from a false matter"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לְבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בית הלל's view from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's rule of calling every bride 'fair and graceful.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For a bride with a clear defect, the praise is untrue, and the תורה forbids falsehood.

steps.title: Praise what someone already bought
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer with a parable: if someone bought a poor item at the market, you praise it to him, you don't put it down.
steps.simpleTranslation: By your logic, if someone bought a bad item at the market, should you praise it to him or criticize it? Obviously, praise it.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל defend their view with an example from everyday life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the purchase is done, criticizing it only hurts the buyer and changes nothing. The same is true of a groom who has already married. Praising her in his eyes is kindness, not the kind of lie the תורה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say (the answer is clear)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵיכֶם, מִי שֶׁלָּקַח מִקָּח רַע מִן הַשּׁוּק,
phrases.english: According to your words, one who bought a bad item from the market,
should one praise it in his eyes, or criticize it in his eyes?
phrases.notes: 'In his eyes' means when talking to the buyer himself, so it looks good or bad to him.

phrases.english: You must say: one should praise it in his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי לְדִבְרֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בית שמאי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parable showing the praise is proper kindness, not forbidden falsehood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling a bride with a defect 'fair' breaks the command to keep far from falsehood.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the choice is final, praising it to the person is the right and kind thing, just as everyone praises a purchase already made.

steps.title: Always be on good terms with people
steps.stepSummary: From בית הלל's answer, the חכמים draw a general lesson: a person should always be pleasant and in tune with others.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here the חכמים said: a person's mind should always be blended with people.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends the argument by turning בית הלל's point into a general rule for how to treat others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson goes beyond weddings. A person should think about how others feel and treat them warmly, the way you would praise someone's purchase or someone's bride.

keyTerms.meaning: Blended with people (in tune with others)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows בית הלל: we call every כלה 'fair and graceful,' because caring for others' feelings is the right way to act.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known rule of good character: be considerate and friendly with everyone.

phrases.english: From here the Sages said:
A person's mind should always be
blended with other people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general lesson from בית הלל's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Always be considerate and pleasant with people, which is why every bride is praised as fair and graceful.

steps.title: The bridal song in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports the song they sing before brides in ארץ ישראל: no makeup, no hair styling, and still graceful.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: this is what they sing before brides in the West: 'No eye makeup, no rouge, no braided hair, and still a graceful doe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on and tells us the actual words sung before a כלה in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The song praises the bride as beautiful without any makeup or styling. It fits בית הלל's style of warm praise for every bride.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
phrases.notes: He came from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing teachings and customs from there.

phrases.english: This is what they sing before brides in the West:
"No eye makeup and no rouge
and no braided hair, and yet a graceful doe."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the actual words of the bridal song used in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל they praised the bride as beautiful without makeup or styling.

steps.title: The same song for רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: When the rabbis gave רבי זירא סמיכה, they sang the same bridal song about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the rabbis ordained רבי זירא, they sang to him: 'No eye makeup, no rouge, no braided hair, and still a graceful doe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: the bridal song was also used to praise a rabbi at his סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words were said about a bride, but here they are used as a picture. They praise רבי זירא as having real beauty and worth without any outer decoration.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סָמְכוּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי זֵירָא, שָׁרוּ לֵיהּ הָכִי:
phrases.english: When the rabbis ordained Rabbi Zeira, they sang to him like this:
"No eye makeup and no rouge
and no braided hair, and yet a graceful doe."
phrases.notes: These are the same words as the bridal song, now sung as praise for a rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the same song from step 5 used to praise a rabbi.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bridal song was sung as praise for רבי זירא at his סמיכה.

steps.title: The song for רבי אמי and רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: At the סמיכה of רבי אמי and רבי אסי they sang: ordain people like these, not people who twist or lack Torah knowledge.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the rabbis ordained רבי אמי and רבי אסי, they sang: 'Anyone like this one and like that one, ordain for us. Don't ordain for us people who twist the law or are worthless.' Some say: 'not those who know only a fifth, and not those with incomplete knowledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another song sung at a סמיכה, this time for two rabbis together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The song praises רבי אמי and רבי אסי by saying: give us more rabbis like them. It also warns against giving סמיכה to people who distort or only partly know the Torah. Two versions of the song's ending are given.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it this way
Those who know only a fifth

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סְמַכוּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּלְרַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: When the rabbis ordained Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
they sang to them like this:

phrases.aramaic: ״כֹּל מִן דֵּין וְכֹל מִן דֵּין סְמוּכוּ לַנָא,
phrases.english: "Anyone like this one and anyone like that one, ordain for us,
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' are רבי אמי and רבי אסי: give us more rabbis like them.

phrases.english: do not ordain for us

phrases.aramaic: לָא מִן סַרְמִיסִין וְלָא מִן סַרְמִיטִין״,
phrases.english: not from those who twist the law and not from the worthless,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: ״לָא מִן חֲמִיסִין וְלָא מִן טוּרְמִיסִין״.
phrases.english: And some say: "Not from those who know only a fifth and not from those with incomplete knowledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סְמַכוּ רַבָּנַן לְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וּלְרַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another song sung at a סמיכה, like the one for רבי זירא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי and רבי אסי were praised as the model of who deserves סמיכה, as opposed to those who distort or only partly know the Torah.

steps.title: The emperor's maids sing for רבי אבהו
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אבהו came to the emperor's house, the maidservants came out and sang his praise as a leader and a light for his people.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אבהו came from the ישיבה to the emperor's house, the emperor's maidservants went out to greet him and sang: 'Great one of his people, leader of his nation, lamp of light, blessed is your coming in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends with one more story of a great rabbi being greeted with a song of praise, this time by non-Jews in the royal house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the servants of the Roman ruler honored רבי אבהו. Their song calls him a leader of his people and a source of light, and blesses his arrival.
steps.whatToRemember: Songs of praise were sung for brides, and in the same way for great rabbis: at their סמיכה, and even by the emperor's servants for רבי אבהו.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Abbahu would come
from the yeshiva to the emperor's house,
the maidservants of the emperor's house would go out to greet him
and they would sing to him like this:
"Great one of his people and leader of his nation,
lamp of light,
blessed is your coming in peace."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ כִּי הֲוָה אָתֵי מִמְּתִיבְתָּא לְבֵי קֵיסָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another example of a song of praise sung for a great rabbi.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The emperor's maidservants greeted רבי אבהו with a song honoring him as leader and light of his people.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי dances before the bride
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר אילעאי would take a הדס branch, dance before the כלה, and praise her as fair and graceful.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי יהודה בר אילעאי that he used to take a myrtle branch, dance in front of the bride, and say: 'A beautiful and graceful bride.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a great תנא who personally danced and sang to make a bride happy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the earlier steps about praising brides. It shows that even a leading sage took part in the simple, joyful מצוה of dancing before the כלה. The words he used, נאה וחסודה, are בית הלל's bridal praise from step 1.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַאי
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Yehuda bar Elai
that he would take a myrtle branch,
and dance before the bride,
and say: "A beautiful and graceful bride."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אִילְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another story of a sage honoring a bride, after the songs in steps 5 to 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great sages personally danced and praised the bride to bring her joy.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק juggles three branches
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק would dance with three branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק would dance with three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of another sage who went even further and danced while juggling three branches. This sets up the reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Juggling is a more playful, less dignified way to dance than holding a single branch. That difference is what bothers רבי זירא in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak
would dance with three.
phrases.notes: He means three myrtle branches, which he would toss and juggle while dancing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מְרַקֵּד אַתְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one level beyond רבי יהודה בר אילעאי's single branch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק danced before brides while juggling three branches.

steps.title: רבי זירא objects that this is embarrassing
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא complains that the old man is embarrassing the Torah scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The old man is embarrassing us.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא criticizes the juggling and says it makes the sages look foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about the dignity of a תלמיד חכם: juggling in public looks undignified. This is a challenge to whether this kind of dancing is proper, and the next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: the old man (here, an elder sage)

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
The old man is embarrassing us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts critically to the juggling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The dignity of רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's juggling before the bride
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah scholar acting playfully in public lowers the honor of all the sages.

steps.title: A pillar of fire honors him at his death
steps.stepSummary: When רב שמואל בר רב יצחק died, a pillar of fire separated him from everyone, a sign given to only one or two people per generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he died, a pillar of fire separated him from everyone else. And we have a tradition that a pillar of fire separates only for one or two people in a generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells what happened when רב שמואל בר רב יצחק died. Heaven showed he was one of the greatest people of his time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story answers רבי זירא's complaint. If Heaven honored him with such a rare sign, his way of dancing could not have been shameful. It actually earned him great reward.

phrases.english: When he died,
phrases.notes: This is רב שמואל בר רב יצחק, the one who juggled.

phrases.english: a pillar of fire separated
between him and everyone else,
and we have a tradition that a pillar of fire does not separate
except either for one person in a generation,
or for two in a generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ אִיפְּסִיק עַמּוּדָא דְנוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's criticism with a sign from Heaven.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the juggling was shameful
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Heaven gave him a rare honor, so his conduct was praiseworthy, not embarrassing.

steps.title: רבי זירא admits the branch earned him reward
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the old man's branch (or his silliness, or his way of doing things) brought him this honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: His branch helped the old man. Some say: His silliness helped the old man. Some say: His way of doing things helped the old man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא, who had complained, now admits that the juggling was the very thing that earned the old man this honor. The גמרא gives three versions of his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three versions sound alike in Aramaic. Whether it was his branch, his 'silly' behavior, or his special way, all versions agree that dancing to gladden the bride was a great merit.
steps.whatToRemember: Making a כלה happy is so important that even behavior that looks undignified can earn a person a rare heavenly reward.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
His branch helped the old man.
And some say: His silliness helped the old man.
And some say: His way of doing things helped the old man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא takes back his complaint from step 11 after the sign in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The juggling to make the bride happy was a merit that earned רב שמואל בר רב יצחק great honor.

steps.title: רב אחא dances with the bride on his shoulders
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא would put the bride on his shoulders and dance.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא would put her on his shoulders and dance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a sage who danced while carrying the bride on his shoulders. This sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes further than the earlier stories, because it involves physical contact with the bride. That is why the חכמים ask in the next step whether they may do the same.

phrases.english: Rav Acha would put her on his shoulders
and dance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא מַרְכֵּיב לַהּ אַכַּתְפֵּיהּ וּמְרַקֵּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story of dancing before a bride, but with physical contact.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא danced while carrying the bride on his shoulders.

steps.title: The חכמים ask if they may do the same
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask רב אחא whether they are allowed to dance this way too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said to him: May we do this too?
steps.whatsHappening: The other sages ask whether רב אחא's way of dancing is allowed for them as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They are not attacking רב אחא. They want to know if this is a general practice that anyone may follow, or something limited.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the rule about doing this?

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:
What about us, may we do this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether רב אחא's practice in step 14 applies to others.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether other sages may also carry the bride on their shoulders and dance.

steps.title: Only if she is like a wooden beam to you
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא answers: if the bride feels to you like a wooden beam, go ahead; if not, you may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If she is like a wooden beam to you, fine. If not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא answers that it depends on the person: only someone who feels no attraction at all may do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The permission is not about the act itself but about the person's inner state. Someone fully free of improper thoughts may dance this way; anyone else may not.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not saying everyone may carry the bride. He is limiting it to someone for whom she is truly like a piece of wood.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If they seem to you like a beam, fine,
phrases.notes: "They" means brides: if carrying one feels no different to you than carrying a wooden beam.

phrases.english: and if not, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is allowed only for someone who feels no attraction to the bride, as if she were a wooden beam.

steps.title: רבי יונתן allows looking at a bride for seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן says one may look at a כלה's face all seven days of celebration, to make her more beloved to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: It is allowed to look at a bride's face all seven days, to make her dear to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling that allows people to look at a bride's face during the seven days of celebration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is that when others admire her, her husband will love her more. This is a new legal ruling, and the next step tells us whether we follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: all seven days (of the wedding celebration)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said that Rabbi Yonatan said:

phrases.aramaic: מוּתָּר לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בִּפְנֵי כַלָּה כׇּל שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.english: It is permitted to look at the face of a bride all seven days,
in order to make her dear to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּתָּר לְהִסְתַּכֵּל בִּפְנֵי כַלָּה כׇּל שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from dancing stories to a legal ruling about looking at a bride.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may look at a bride's face during the seven days of celebration to increase her husband's love.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רבי יונתן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רבי יונתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us that we do not follow רבי יונתן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though his reason sounds nice, the final הלכה does not allow looking at a bride's face. She is a married woman, and the usual rules still apply to her.

keyTerms.meaning: the הלכה is not like him

steps.whatToRemember: The stories praise bringing joy to a כלה, but the הלכה still keeps the limits: we do not follow רבי יונתן's permission to gaze at a bride.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not like him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final ruling on רבי יונתן's statement in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: It is not permitted to gaze at a bride's face, even during the seven days of celebration.

steps.title: A funeral moves aside for a bride, and both move aside for a king
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a funeral procession gives way to a כלה, and both give way to a Jewish king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A funeral procession moves aside for a bride. And both of them move aside for a king of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets an order of who gives way to whom on the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wedding procession comes before a funeral procession. A Jewish king comes before both of them. This ranking is the base for the story about the king and the question that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: a dead person (here, the funeral procession)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One moves the dead aside before a bride.
phrases.notes: The dead person isn't moved alone. The whole funeral procession turns aside so the wedding procession can pass.

phrases.english: And both this and that before a king of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲבִירִין אֶת הַמֵּת מִלִּפְנֵי כַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of honoring a כלה, now in a ruling about who gives way on the road.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Funeral gives way to a כלה; both give way to a Jewish king.

steps.title: King Agrippas moved aside for a bride and was praised
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells that אגריפס המלך gave way to a כלה, and the חכמים praised him.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about King Agrippas that he moved aside for a bride, and the Sages praised him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story about a king who gave way to a כלה even though the rule says she gives way to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the rule in the last step, the כלה should have made way for the king. אגריפס did the opposite, and the חכמים praised him for it. This seems to clash with the rule, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

phrases.english: They said about King Agrippas
that he moved aside before a bride,
and the Sages praised him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that seems to go against the rule just given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אגריפס yielded to a כלה and the חכמים praised him.

steps.title: How can a king be praised for giving up his honor?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the praise, because רב אשי taught that a king may not give up his honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: They praised him? That means he did the right thing? But רב אשי said: even according to the one who says a נשיא may give up his honor, a king may not give up his honor. As the Torah says, 'You shall surely set a king over you,' which means his awe must be upon you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the story. If a king is not allowed to give up his honor, why did the חכמים praise אגריפס for doing exactly that?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי teaches that a king's honor is not his own to give away. The פסוק makes fear of the king part of what kingship is. So yielding to a כלה should be wrong, not praiseworthy.

keyTerms.meaning: does that imply he acted well?
gave up the honor owed to him

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying a king must be proud. He is saying the honor belongs to the role the Torah set up, so the king personally cannot cancel it. A נשיא can give up his honor (according to one view), but a king cannot.

phrases.english: They praised him? That implies he did well?
But didn't Rav Ashi say:
Even according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׂיא שֶׁמָּחַל עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ — כְּבוֹדוֹ מָחוּל,
phrases.english: a Nasi who gives up his honor, his honor is given up,
a king who gives up his honor,
his honor is not given up.
As the Master said:
"You shall surely set a king over you"
that his awe should be upon you!

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁבְּחוּהוּ — מִכְּלָל דְּשַׁפִּיר עֲבַד? וְהָא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the praise given to אגריפס in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' praise of אגריפס for yielding to a כלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A king may not give up his honor (רב אשי, based on the פסוק). So yielding should be forbidden, not praised.

steps.title: It happened at a crossroads
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the meeting was at a crossroads, so the king's honor was not visibly lowered.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was at a crossroads.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a short reply: the event took place at a fork in the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At a crossroads, onlookers could not tell that the king turned aside for the כלה. It could look like he simply chose a different road. So his honor was never publicly given up, and he was still praised for his kind intention.

keyTerms.meaning: a crossroads, a fork in the road

phrases.english: It was a crossroads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against the story.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the facts of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The king openly yielded to the כלה and so gave up his honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: At a crossroads his yielding was not noticeable, so his honor stayed whole.
steps.whatToRemember: A king may not give up his honor. אגריפס was praised only because, at a crossroads, nobody could see that he had yielded.

steps.title: Stopping Torah study for a funeral or a bride
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one stops תלמוד תורה to escort the dead and to bring a כלה to her wedding, and רבי יהודה בר אלעאי did this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: One stops Torah study to carry out the dead for burial and to bring a bride to her wedding. They said about רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי that he would stop Torah study to carry out the dead and to bring in a bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא: escorting the dead and celebrating a כלה are important enough to stop learning for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually nothing interrupts תלמוד תורה. Here two acts of kindness, burying the dead and bringing a כלה to her wedding, push it aside. The story of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי shows a great scholar actually living this way.

keyTerms.meaning: carrying out the dead for burial
bringing a bride in to her wedding

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One stops Torah study
for carrying out the dead and for bringing in a bride.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִלְעַאי
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Ilai
that he would stop Torah study
for carrying out the dead and for bringing in a bride.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְבַטְּלִין תַּלְמוּד תּוֹרָה לְהוֹצָאַת הַמֵּת וּלְהַכְנָסַת כַּלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ברייתא on the same pair, the dead and the כלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One interrupts Torah study to escort the dead or a כלה.

steps.title: Only when there are not enough people already
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule: one stops learning only if the dead person does not yet have all the honor he needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: When were these words said? When there are not enough people with him for all his needs. But if there are enough people with him for all his needs, one does not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a limit: you only interrupt your learning if more people are still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is not that every learner stops for every funeral. If the dead person already has a proper crowd honoring him, the learners keep learning. This raises the obvious question of how big a crowd is 'enough.'

keyTerms.meaning: in what case was this said?
all that he needs (enough people to honor him)

phrases.english: When were these words said?
When he does not have with him all he needs.
But if he has with him all he needs,
one does not stop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule of stopping Torah study.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One stops learning only if the proper number of people is not yet there.

steps.title: How many people count as 'enough'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what number of people counts as 'all his needs.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And how many is 'all his needs'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the answers that follow: how big a crowd is enough?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a limit but no number. The גמרא wants a measure, so a person knows when he must stop learning and when he may keep going.

phrases.english: And how much is "all he needs"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure behind the limit just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of people that counts as 'all his needs'

steps.title: Twelve or thirteen thousand men with שופרות
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר איני in the name of רב gives a number: 12,000 men plus 6,000 with שופרות, or by another version 13,000 men, 6,000 of them with שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר איני said in the name of רב: twelve thousand men and six thousand שופרות. Some report it this way: thirteen thousand men, and among them six thousand שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first answer, a set number of people, and reports two versions of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version the 6,000 shofar blowers are added on top of the 12,000 men. In the second version the total is 13,000, and the 6,000 shofar blowers are counted inside it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Ini said in the name of Rav:
Twelve thousand men,
and six thousand shofars.
And some say it:
Thirteen thousand men,
and among them six thousand shofars.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of how many.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 12,000 men plus 6,000 shofars, or 13,000 men including 6,000 shofars

steps.title: A line of people from the city gate to the cemetery
steps.stepSummary: עולא measures 'enough' as a crowd that stretches like a wall from the city gate to the burial place.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: for example, when the men form a wall from the city gate all the way to the cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer. עולא measures by distance instead of by a number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא does not give a count. He says there are enough people when they fill the whole route, from the gate of the city to the burial place.

keyTerms.meaning: they form a partition, a wall

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Such as when the men form a wall
from the city gate until the cemetery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Enough men to line the route from the city gate to the burial place

steps.title: Taking away the Torah needs as many as receiving it
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת (or רבי יוחנן) says the Torah's 'taking away' at a scholar's death needs 600,000 people, the same as at its giving at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת, and some say רבי יוחנן, said: its taking is like its giving. Just as its giving was with six hundred thousand, so too its taking is with six hundred thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third answer, the largest one, based on a comparison to מתן תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a Torah scholar dies, the Torah he held is 'taken' from the world. Since the Torah was given in front of 600,000 people at סיני, its taking needs the same number for full honor.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (it was a different speaker)

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, and some say Rabbi Yochanan, said:
Its taking is like its giving,
phrases.notes: "Its" means the Torah's. When a Torah scholar dies, the Torah he carried is taken from the world.

phrases.english: just as its giving was with six hundred thousand,
so too its taking is with six hundred thousand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: נְטִילָתָהּ — כִּנְתִינָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer, based on a comparison to סיני.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 600,000 people, like the number at מתן תורה

steps.title: This applies to someone who learned מקרא and משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to limit the 600,000 rule to a person who read and studied Torah. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies to one who read and studied,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to explain which kind of person gets the 600,000 measure. This line sets up a contrast that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large number belongs to someone who learned מקרא and משנה, because the Torah he carried is being 'taken.' The sentence is not finished yet. The גמרא is about to compare him to another kind of scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: and these words apply only to
who read מקרא and studied משנה

phrases.english: And these words apply to one who read and studied,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to limit the 600,000 measure from the last step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 600,000 measure applies to one who studied מקרא and משנה (the sentence continues next).
